meta.title: Deterministic games in Fizlet: seeds and lockstep
meta.description: Make a Fizlet sim replay from a seed: fixed step, seeded random, typed arrays and input bits. syncCheck finds the first frame where two peers differ.

ld.headline: Same seed,
ld.description: Make a Fizlet sim replay from a seed: fixed step, seeded random, typed arrays and input bits. syncCheck finds the first frame where two peers differ.

lead: A Fizlet sim that steps on a fixed dt, draws every random number from engine.random and keeps its state in typed arrays replays exactly from a seed. That is what makes a replay test possible, and what lets two players run the same game in lockstep with only their inputs crossing the wire.

body.html:
The rules for a deterministic step

  • Seeded random only. engine.random() is seeded by createEngine({ seed }) and allocation-free; engine.random.state snapshots and restores it. No Math.random in the step.
  • No clock in the step. Use dt and engine.steps (an integer count of fixed steps), never performance.now() or Date.
  • No layout reads. A sim that reads the page depends on the screen. In net play, fix the arena size and scale the drawing.
  • Inputs as bits. Pack what a player does into one 32-bit word per frame; the step reads only the words.
  • Nothing else moves on engine steps. Anything that advances with the step (a drop timer, a random draw in an effect) must advance on the same frames on every peer.

body.label: SYNC CHECK · sync.test.ts

body.html:
syncCheck: find the first frame that differs

syncCheck(setup, { players, frames, latency, jitter }) from @fzlt/core/presence/check runs your sim as lockstep clients over an in-memory link with the latency and jitter you ask for, hashes each client's state every frame and returns { ok, frames, diverged, stalls }. diverged is the first frame whose state differed, or -1. It is test-only code (4,870 B gzip) and never ships to players.

The presence brick's own tests run two clients byte-identical for 3,000 frames with no latency, stay identical with delayed, jittered and reordered inputs at unequal frame rates, run four players at latency 3, and catch a forced desync at the next hash check.
